name: Curiora Campus
description: Curio is the local AI prototype within Curiora Campus: a FastAPI backend, shared model gateway, and conversation interface. Text → GPT-OSS 20B. Vision / Multimodal → Qwen3-VL 8B. Both are pretrained model integrations.
question: How can a campus-oriented interface accept text and images through one understandable local AI backend?

capabilities.text: Routes text to pretrained GPT-OSS 20B and image requests to pretrained Qwen3-VL 8B through a shared model gateway.
Includes MLX on Apple Silicon and PyTorch CUDA/CPU runtime adapters, with hardware detection and adapter selection implemented in code.
Uses lazy loading, gateway locks, and unloading of the previous model before switching between text and vision modes.
Accepts text/image requests through an async FastAPI endpoint, checks declared image type and upload size, dispatches blocking inference to a thread pool, and removes temporary images.
Assigns conversation IDs and keeps text-message history in process memory for subsequent model prompts.
Provides browser image uploads, camera-still capture, and browser speech input around the conversation interface.

approach: Keep the interface, model gateway, and runtime adapters separate, and account for model memory constraints when switching modes.
limitations: This is a local prototype reviewed through source code. Cross-platform execution, performance, and production deployment have not been validated.
Model IDs are configured in code; eager MLX imports limit claims of universal CPU/CUDA startup.
Conversation history is process-local text. Durable memory, persistent image history, continuous video analysis, retrieval, tool execution, and independent outcome verification are not implemented.
The wider campus authentication, database, and reporting workflows remain scaffolded.

implemented.note: The active request path adds process-memory conversation text before dispatch and calls the model gateway directly. This describes code structure, not a deployment or benchmark result.

stages.name: Perceive
stages.scope: Image input, camera stills, and vision-language inference.

stages.name: Understand
stages.scope: Prompted text and image responses; no separate semantic planning layer.

stages.name: Route
stages.scope: Modality and hardware routing; task and tool routing remain planned.

stages.name: Act
stages.scope: Tool execution and external action orchestration are not implemented.

stages.name: Verify
stages.scope: Independent factual and external-outcome verification are not implemented; input checks are a separate current capability.

name: Curiora Pay
description: A Python, FastAPI, and PostgreSQL banking-workflow prototype with session-based routes, transaction operations, pandas CSV statement generation, and a logistic-regression learning demonstration using synthetic data.
question: How can transaction workflows produce queryable data, useful statements, and features for a small classification exercise?

capabilities.text: Implements session-based login and protected dashboard routes, with parameterized credential queries and Argon2 password verification.
Implements account creation, balance retrieval, deposits, withdrawals, internal transfers, and transaction records through synchronous PostgreSQL/Psycopg operations.
Queries account transactions with SQL, builds a pandas dataframe, and writes CSV statements on the server.
Retrieves account balance and SQL-derived transaction count, then constructs a NumPy feature array for model prediction.
Fits a scikit-learn logistic-regression demonstration on eight synthetic examples. It is a learning exercise with no held-out evaluation or validated lending performance.
Uses Fernet encryption for stored transaction notes.

approach: Keep data retrieval, business rules, and model assumptions explicit so a learning experiment remains understandable alongside the backend that supplies its features.
limitations: This is a banking-workflow prototype, not a production bank, payment-network integration, or security/concurrency-audited system.
Request handlers and business operations are synchronous. A separate Psycopg AsyncConnection schema-setup helper is incomplete and is not wired into application startup.
Statement generation writes a local CSV; the current route returns an HTML message rather than downloading the file. The dedicated transaction-history route is unfinished.
The classifier uses hand-coded synthetic rows without held-out evaluation. Accuracy, repayment probability, or real credit-risk validity are not established.

models.name: Logistic regression
models.training_data: Eight hand-coded examples with balance and transaction-count features

name: Curiora Research
description: A local visual-intelligence experiment integrating pretrained Qwen3-VL 8B through MLX and FastAPI, with lazy model loading, serialized inference, and prompts requesting image-grounded answers and explicit uncertainty.
question: How can a local vision-language model answer questions about an image while making uncertainty explicit?

capabilities.text: Integrates pretrained Qwen3-VL 8B through MLX behind a FastAPI image-analysis endpoint.
Uses lazy model loading, a model-loading lock, and an inference lock that serializes generation.
Prompts the model to use visible image evidence and acknowledge uncertainty; this is a prompting strategy rather than an independent verifier.
Validates image uploads, dispatches analysis to a thread pool, and cleans up temporary image files.
Provides image upload, camera-preview/still-image input, and browser speech-input interfaces.

approach: Study the interaction between image input, prompting, model lifecycle, and interface while keeping the scope of each experiment clear.
limitations: This is a local image-inference experiment using an external pretrained model; foundation-model training, benchmarks, and production serving are not claimed.
Camera preview does not establish continuous video analysis. Research-agent and intelligent-reasoning features remain a roadmap.
Grounded prompting does not guarantee factual accuracy or independently verify an outcome.

name: The foundations matter.
description: Python problem solving, small asynchronous web-server exercises, SQL data preparation, and classification fundamentals developed through project practice.
question: What changes when I implement a small version of an idea and inspect how it works?

capabilities.text: Practices Python problem solving and small ASGI routing and asynchronous request-handler exercises.
Practices SQL queries, pandas dataframes, NumPy feature arrays, and logistic-regression fundamentals through local project work.

approach: Start with a question, build a small version, inspect its behavior, and use the result to guide the next iteration.
limitations: This is a collection of learning exercises, not an additional product, internship, or original research result. The link opens the GitHub profile; it does not imply every local exercise is published.

name: Curiora Design System
description: Shared CSS tokens, glass surfaces, reusable components, and a pointer-reactive Curio signature for the Curiora visual language.
question: How can related Curiora experiments share a coherent visual language?

capabilities.text: Defines typography, spacing, color and glass tokens, UI components, and a reduced-motion-aware pointer signature.

approach: Reuse shared visual primitives across product experiments.
limitations: Documentation files are largely empty; this is not a comprehensively documented component library.

name: Curiora Website
description: A FastAPI/Jinja2 landing-page prototype introducing the Curiora ecosystem with responsive product storytelling and its glass-and-orbit identity.
question: How can the Curiora ecosystem and its guiding ideas be explained clearly?

capabilities.text: Uses FastAPI/Jinja2 templates, responsive layouts, scroll reveals, and a glass-and-orbit visual signature.

approach: Connect each project to the wider idea that curiosity creates intelligence.
limitations: Some product links are placeholders and secondary routes reference missing templates; a complete published site is not established.
